english.title: Publish prohibited statement of an exit poll - elections
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), at

(A)_[a parliamentary election]_
(B)_[a local government election]_

published before the poll had closed, a statement relating to the way in which voters had voted at the election where that statement was, or might reasonably be taken to have been, based on information given by voters after they had voted.
english.legislation: Contrary to section 66A(1)(a) and (3) of the Representation of the People Act 1983.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
publish
before the poll is closed
any statement relating to the way in which voters have voted
at the election where that statement is based on information
given by voters after they have voted

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See Section 65A(2) for the definition of a relevant election as it applies to this offence.
(ii) See Section 66A(4) for the definition of "publish"
(iii) This offence has been inserted by paragraph 6 of Schedule 6 of the Representation of the People Act 2000.
(iv) See H2690 for publish prohibited forecast of election result.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
